trial_court: Court of Sh. Surinder S. Rathi, District Judge (Comm.)-03 Shahdara, KKD, Delhi
case_name: Icici Bank Ltd vs Kapil Kumar

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: ICICI Bank Limited, a nationalized bank (plaintiff)
parties.respondent_defendant: Kapil Kumar, s/o Sh. Ramesh Chandra (defendant)

facts_of_case: Defendant approached ICICI Bank for an auto loan to purchase a Honda City Car. The bank sanctioned the loan but the defendant defaulted on payments. The bank issued a foreclosure notice and filed this suit seeking recovery of Rs.8,60,840/- along with interest.

legal_principles.principle: Where any party fails to present a written statement called for by the Court, the Court shall pronounce judgment against him or make such order in relation to the suit as it thinks fit.
legal_principles.held: The Court shall pronounce judgment against him, or make such order in relation to the suit as it thinks fit and on the pronouncement of such judgment a decree shall be drawn up.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 — Order 8 Rule 10

legal_principles.principle: In the absence of any pleadings on behalf of the defendant, the case of the plaintiff is deemed to be admitted.
legal_principles.held: The pleadings of the plaintiff has remained unrebutted, unchallenged and uncontroverted. In the absence of any pleadings on behalf of defendant, case of the plaintiff is deemed to be admitted.
cited_cases: ICICI Bank Ltd vs Kapil Kumar

legal_principles.principle: The documents maintained by a bank in the ordinary course of its business can be considered to be duly executed in due course of the business and capable of binding the parties into a contractual relationship.
legal_principles.held: Though the exceptions cannot be ruled out, but generally taking a judicial notice of the banking business, these documents can be considered to be duly executed in due course of the business and capable of binding the parties into a contractual relationship.
cited_cases: ICICI Bank Ltd vs Kapil Kumar

outcome.final_order: The court decreed the suit in favour of ICICI Bank Limited, ordering the defendant to pay Rs.8,60,840/- along with interest @24% per annum.
